:::{#thm-de-morgan-logic}
#### De Morgan's laws for propositions

For any [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $Q$
[@wikipedia_de_morgans_laws]:

$$
\ba
\neg (P \land Q) &\equiv \neg P \lor \neg Q \\
\neg (P \lor Q) &\equiv \neg P \land \neg Q
\ea
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

Each side of each law is built from $P$ and $Q$,
so by @def-logically-equivalent
it is enough to compare the two sides in each of the four rows of a [truth table](#def-truth-table):

| $P$ | $Q$ | $\neg (P \land Q)$ | $\neg P \lor \neg Q$ | $\neg (P \lor Q)$ | $\neg P \land \neg Q$ |
|:---:|:---:|:------------------:|:--------------------:|:-----------------:|:---------------------:|
| T   | T   | F                  | F                    | F                 | F                     |
| T   | F   | T                  | T                    | F                 | F                     |
| F   | T   | T                  | T                    | F                 | F                     |
| F   | F   | T                  | T                    | T                 | T                     |

The third and fourth columns agree in every row,
which proves the first law,
and the fifth and sixth columns agree in every row,
which proves the second.

:::

:::
